# ToolbarControlGroup

<!-- Generated by scripts/sync-component-docs.mjs from ai/component-catalog.json and ai/component-composition.json. Do not edit; run `npm run catalog:sync`. -->

`@kerfjs/ui:toolbar-control-group` · Kerf UI · component · Structure

Typed toolbar groups for buttons, semantic action links, compact mixed controls, selected states, dropdown surfaces, and avatar controls.

## When to use

Provide complete toolbar action geometry through configuration, including semantic anchors, overflow containment, and dropdown menu insets without application CSS.

- Group related controls inside a toolbar with a supported visual treatment.
- Use ToolbarActionLink for navigation or external resources that must retain native anchor semantics inside a group.
- Fill it with plain \<button> controls (the group styles > button fully); use wa-button only for a Web Awesome feature. A popup menu is a PopupMenu in a single group with nestedDropdown; it renders its own trigger, so never hand-write wa-dropdown markup. Each control stays whole: an icon sits beside its label on one row and no trigger gets a fixed width. Use overflow=wrap for independent links that should move as whole actions to another row on narrow surfaces.
- For an avatar control, set content=avatar and avatarImage instead of inserting an img; one button paints the group and multiple buttons paint only the pressed highlight.
- In a Workbench or CollapsiblePanel toolbar, mark a group relocateOnCollapse to keep it available in the work-area toolbar when the panel closes; place it directly or in an array in any toolbar zone.

**Not when:**

- Do not use merely to align unrelated buttons or to imitate an exclusive choice.
- Do not reach for wa-button for an ordinary control inside the group — a plain \<button> is the default and avoids the Web Awesome dependency.

**Alternatives:**

- [SegmentedControl](./segmented-control.md) (nearest)
- [Button Group](./wa-button-group.md) (prefer-over)

## Imports

- JavaScript: `@kerfjs/ui/toolbar-control-group` — exports `ToolbarActionLink`, `ToolbarControlGroup`.
- CSS: the browser build of `@kerfjs/ui/toolbar-control-group` pulls its CSS automatically; import `@kerfjs/ui/toolbar-control-group.css` manually only without the `browser` export condition.
- Declared side effects: browser-condition-css.

## Composition

- Parents: only inside [Toolbar](./toolbar.md) or [FloatingToolbar](./floating-toolbar.md).
- Contexts: `toolbar-zone`.
- Children: only `control` (required: `control`).
- Built from: [LucideIcon](./lucide-icon.md), [SegmentedControl](./segmented-control.md).

Zones (a zone is bound to JSX only through its listed prop; never assume the zone id is a prop):

- `controls` — no declared JSX prop; accepts `control`; at least 1.

## State and wiring

**The app owns:** actions; link destination and copy; pressed state; expanded state; avatar image URL.

No wiring helper.

## Geometry

Margin: none · border: self · padding: self (layout role: structure). `self` means the component already owns it — do not add wrapper padding, margin, or borders around it.

## Accessibility

- Name the group when its relationship is not evident from context.
- Name an icon-only button or link with aria-label, not title. Once any help-tag installer is imported (select/register, popup-menu/register, or help-tags/register), it shows an aria-hidden Web Awesome help tag repeating that name after a 500ms hover and at once on keyboard focus, hidden on a press and on Escape, and never joins aria-labelledby. A native title keeps the browser tooltip and gets no second tag.

## Styling boundary

The component owns its own styles. Configure it through its props and variants; do not override its internals.

Public class hooks (select for layout placement only, never to change the component's look): `kui-toolbar-action-link`, `kui-toolbar-control-group`.

Never put `kui-toolbar-action-link` on an element you write; render `ToolbarActionLink` instead (`KUI-L103`).

Never put `kui-toolbar-control-group` on an element you write; render `ToolbarControlGroup` instead (`KUI-L103`).

Public tokens it reads: `--kui-color-brand-on-quiet`, `--kui-color-pop-border-normal`, `--kui-color-pop-fill-normal`, `--kui-color-pop-on-normal`, `--kui-color-pop-on-quiet`, `--kui-color-neutral-border-loud`, `--kui-color-neutral-border-normal`, `--kui-color-neutral-fill-loud`, `--kui-color-neutral-fill-normal`, `--kui-color-neutral-on-loud`, `--kui-color-neutral-on-quiet`, `--kui-color-surface`, `--kui-focus-ring`, `--kui-shadow-s`, `--kui-toolbar-control-background`, `--kui-toolbar-control-border`, `--kui-toolbar-control-color`, `--kui-toolbar-control-dark-border`, `--kui-toolbar-control-hover-background`, `--kui-toolbar-control-pressed-background`, `--kui-toolbar-control-pressed-border`, `--kui-toolbar-control-pressed-color`, `--kui-toolbar-control-selected-background`, `--kui-toolbar-control-selected-color`, `--kui-toolbar-control-selected-shadow`.
